claims.text: Pre-depositing aluminum and thermally oxidizing it to form an alumina scale enhances the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The aluminum pretreatment produces a uniform Al2O3 scale.
The alumina scale is an effective diffusion barrier against oxygen attack.
The intervention consists of depositing a thin aluminum coating and then using controlled thermal oxidation to form continuous Al2O3.
The intervention should work at approximately 1000 °C in air or pure oxygen for 100–200 hours.
The resulting Al2O3 layer is continuous and adherent.
The introduced aluminum oxidizes preferentially to form alumina.
The alumina scale is stable under the proposed exposure conditions.
The alumina barrier limits oxygen ingress into the underlying alloy and thereby reduces oxidation kinetics.
Treated samples will gain significantly less weight than untreated samples under identical oxidizing conditions.
Treated samples will develop thinner oxide layers than untreated samples.
Treated samples will retain mechanical integrity better than untreated samples.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys exhibit higher oxidation rates, thicker oxide scales, and greater weight gain under the specified conditions.
Nonuniform alumina formation or inadequate scale adherence can limit the treatment's effectiveness.
Temperatures above the stability range of Al2O3 can cause scale spallation or phase transformations.
